# TIRAI

> TIRAI is an agent skill and Python CLI (`tirai`) that records test evidence. You write a test scenario
> (steps, each with actions and expected results); TIRAI runs it in a real Chrome/Edge browser through
> vercel-labs agent-browser (default) or Tencent BrowserSkill, checks the database in a second browser tab (DBX web) plus a read-only SQL query,
> draws Snagit-style annotations on the page, records each tab, and uses ffmpeg to compose one MP4 with
> a header bar, PASS/FAIL badges and burned-in subtitles, plus a Markdown step report.

TIRAI is an orchestration layer, not a browser or database tool:

- Browser control, screenshots and per-tab MP4 recording: agent-browser (default; single binary, Chrome for Testing) or Tencent BrowserSkill (`bsk` CLI + browser extension). Select with `driver:` / `--driver`.
- Database UI in the browser: DBX web (`t8y2/dbx`, port 4224, 100+ engines).
- TIRAI: scenario format, dry-run and record runner, DOM and read-only DB assertions, injected annotation
  overlay (`annotate.js`), timeline, subtitle generation, video composition, report.

Workflow (always in this order): `tirai validate` → `tirai run --dry-run` (no video, every step must pass)
→ `tirai record` (dry-run again, record one segment per tab, compose) → hand over `evidence/record/final.mp4`
and `report.md` / `report.html` / `report.xlsx`, plus `manifest.sha256` (`tirai verify` detects edited evidence).
`tirai record --record-failures` records a failing run as bug evidence.

Key facts for agents:

- Install: macOS/Linux `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2tsoftwareapp/TIRAI/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --yes`;
  Windows `$env:TIRAI_SETUP_ARGS="--yes"; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2tsoftwareapp/TIRAI/main/install.ps1 | iex`.
  No Python prerequisite: the installer downloads the prebuilt `tirai-<os>-<arch>` binary from GitHub Releases
  when one exists, otherwise builds from source with Python >= 3.10, or with uv + a private Python 3.12 in `~/.tirai`
  when the machine has no suitable Python (`--binary` / `--source` force a method). It links `tirai` into
  `~/.local/bin` and runs `tirai setup` (ffmpeg >= 6.0, upgraded to a static build when older; agent-browser binary + Chrome for Testing; DBX web package or Docker image; BrowserSkill CLI; agent skills). `tirai dbx -d` starts DBX web.
- Only `driver: bsk` needs the BrowserSkill browser extension, installed by the human.
- `tirai setup` downloads pinned, SHA-256-verified agent-browser, DBX web and ffmpeg builds.
- `dbx.connect:` on a DBX tab (or `tirai dbx-connect`) creates the DBX connection from the scenario DSN.
  Never automate it. Never run `sudo` without asking; if a package install needs a password, ask the user.
- Verify with `tirai doctor`: every required check must be `ok` before running scenarios.
- Secrets only as `${ENV_VAR}` in scenarios; values live in the environment or a git-ignored `.env` next to
  the scenario (loaded automatically, or `--env-file`). Secrets are never written to timelines or reports.
- Database checks use a read-only user. DBX renders result cells on a canvas, so `expect: db` runs its own
  read-only query (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite) and annotations target DBX cells with `{ grid: {...} }`.
- Find selectors with `agent-browser snapshot` (or `bsk snapshot`); do not guess. A missing selector, annotation target
  or env var fails the step (fail closed).
- Supported agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, Devin (`tirai install-skill --agent <name>`).

## Source: `tirai --help`

```text
usage: tirai [-h] [--version]
             {doctor,setup,init,validate,run,inspect,compose,record,install-skill,export,scan-pii,index,sign,verify,from-trace,from-spec,capture,dbx,dbx-connect,mcp,annotate-js} ...

Scenario-driven test evidence recorder

positional arguments:
  {doctor,setup,init,validate,run,inspect,compose,record,install-skill,export,scan-pii,index,sign,verify,from-trace,from-spec,capture,dbx,dbx-connect,mcp,annotate-js}
    doctor              check ffmpeg, BrowserSkill, fonts and optional drivers
    setup               install what is missing (ffmpeg, agent-browser, DBX, skills); reuses tools
                        already here
    init                write a scenario template
    validate            validate a scenario file
    run                 run a scenario (--dry-run or --record)
    inspect             list each step's page elements with locators + a suggested targets: block
    compose             build final.mp4 + subtitles + report from a recorded timeline
    record              dry-run, record, then compose in one go
    install-skill       install the tirai-evidence skill for an agent
    export              write junit.xml, xray.json, testrail.csv from an evidence folder (no
                        upload)
    scan-pii            OCR the final video for PII the page masking missed (--fix blurs it)
    index               one HTML page listing every evidence folder found under DIRS
    sign                sign manifest.sha256 with an SSH key (+ optional RFC 3161 timestamp)
    verify              check an evidence folder against its manifest.sha256 (and signature)
    from-trace          convert a `bsk record` trace into a scenario
    from-spec           draft a scenario from a Gherkin .feature, Markdown table or CSV test cases
    capture             record a flow you click through once and turn it into a scenario
    dbx                 start DBX web (installed by `tirai setup`, else Docker)
    dbx-connect         create/update a DBX web connection from a DSN (no manual DBX setup)
    mcp                 run the TIRAI MCP server on stdio (for MCP-capable agents)
    annotate-js         print the path of the injectable annotate.js

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit

usage: tirai doctor [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

usage: tirai setup [-h] [--agent {claude,codex,antigravity,cursor,devin,agents,all}]
                   [--project PROJECT] [--skip SKIP [SKIP ...]] [--only ONLY [ONLY ...]] [--yes]
                   [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent {claude,codex,antigravity,cursor,devin,agents,all}
                        agents to install the skill for (default: detected ones)
  --project PROJECT     install skills into this project instead of the user profile
  --skip SKIP [SKIP ...]
                        ffmpeg, agent-browser, dbx, browserskill, skills (comma or space
                        separated)
  --only ONLY [ONLY ...]
                        run only these steps (same names)
  --yes, -y             install without prompting
  --dry-run             print what would be installed

usage: tirai init [-h] [--force] [path]

positional arguments:
  path

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --force

usage: tirai validate [-h] [--env-file ENV_FILE] [--no-db-check] scenario

positional arguments:
  scenario

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --env-file ENV_FILE  KEY=VALUE file (default: .env next to the scenario)
  --no-db-check        don't connect to check the DSNs are read-only

usage: tirai run [-h] [--env-file ENV_FILE] [--out OUT] [--driver {agent-browser,bsk}] [--headed]
                 [--session SESSION] [--scope SCOPE] [--hold HOLD] [--fresh] [--keep-session]
                 [--allow-writes] [--until STEP] [--from-step STEP] (--dry-run | --record)
                 scenario

positional arguments:
  scenario

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --env-file ENV_FILE   KEY=VALUE file (default: .env next to the scenario)
  --out OUT             output root (default: evidence/)
  --driver {agent-browser,bsk}
                        browser driver (default: agent-browser)
  --headed              show the agent-browser window (default: headless)
  --session SESSION     reuse a live driver session instead of opening a fresh one
  --scope SCOPE         session name prefix for the fresh session
  --hold HOLD           seconds each step stays on screen
  --fresh               clear cookies and storage before tab setup (clean login)
  --keep-session        leave the browser session open afterwards (for --from-step)
  --allow-writes        dry-run: also run steps that write data (writes:, write SQL)
  --until STEP          dry-run: stop after this step
  --from-step STEP      dry-run: start at this step in --session's open page
  --dry-run
  --record

usage: tirai inspect [-h] [--env-file ENV_FILE] [--out OUT] [--driver {agent-browser,bsk}]
                     [--headed] [--session SESSION]
                     scenario

positional arguments:
  scenario              scenario file, or a URL to inspect a single page

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --env-file ENV_FILE   KEY=VALUE file (default: .env next to the scenario)
  --out OUT             output root; writes <out>/inspect/ (default: evidence/)
  --driver {agent-browser,bsk}
                        browser driver (default: agent-browser)
  --headed              show the agent-browser window
  --session SESSION     reuse a live driver session

usage: tirai compose [-h] [--output OUTPUT] [--lead LEAD] [--title-seconds TITLE_SECONDS]
                     [--lang LANG] [--voice [{auto,say,sapi,espeak,cmd}]] [--trim-still]
                     timeline

positional arguments:
  timeline

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT       final video path (default: <timeline dir>/final.mp4)
  --lead LEAD           seconds kept before each step starts
  --title-seconds TITLE_SECONDS
  --lang LANG           subtitle language to burn in (from per-step subtitle maps)
  --voice [{auto,say,sapi,espeak,cmd}]
                        read each subtitle aloud (OS speech engine) and add it as the video's
                        audio track
  --trim-still          fast-forward (8x, badge shown) stretches where the screen does not change
                        for 2 s or more

usage: tirai record [-h] [--env-file ENV_FILE] [--out OUT] [--driver {agent-browser,bsk}]

                    [--output OUTPUT] [--lead LEAD] [--title-seconds TITLE_SECONDS] [--lang LANG]
                    [--voice [{auto,say,sapi,espeak,cmd}]] [--trim-still] [--skip-dry-run]
                    [--record-failures]
                    scenario

positional arguments:
  scenario

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --env-file ENV_FILE   KEY=VALUE file (default: .env next to the scenario)
  --out OUT             output root (default: evidence/)
  --driver {agent-browser,bsk}
                        browser driver (default: agent-browser)
  --headed              show the agent-browser window (default: headless)
  --session SESSION     reuse a live driver session instead of opening a fresh one
  --scope SCOPE         session name prefix for the fresh session
  --hold HOLD           seconds each step stays on screen
  --fresh               clear cookies and storage before tab setup (clean login)
  --keep-session        leave the browser session open afterwards (for --from-step)
  --allow-writes        dry-run: also run steps that write data (writes:, write SQL)
  --until STEP          dry-run: stop after this step
  --from-step STEP      dry-run: start at this step in --session's open page
  --output OUTPUT       final video path (default: <timeline dir>/final.mp4)
  --lead LEAD           seconds kept before each step starts
  --title-seconds TITLE_SECONDS
  --lang LANG           subtitle language to burn in (from per-step subtitle maps)
  --voice [{auto,say,sapi,espeak,cmd}]
                        read each subtitle aloud (OS speech engine) and add it as the video's
                        audio track
  --trim-still          fast-forward (8x, badge shown) stretches where the screen does not change
                        for 2 s or more
  --skip-dry-run
  --record-failures     record and compose even when a step fails (bug evidence)

usage: tirai install-skill [-h] --agent {claude,codex,antigravity,cursor,devin,agents,all}
                           [--project PROJECT] [--dest DEST] [--force]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent {claude,codex,antigravity,cursor,devin,agents,all}
  --project PROJECT     install into this project instead of the user profile
  --dest DEST           explicit skills directory (overrides --agent paths)

usage: tirai export [-h] [--format FORMAT [FORMAT ...]] [--test-key TEST_KEY]
                    [--project-key PROJECT_KEY] [--case-id CASE_ID]
                    [dir]

positional arguments:
  dir

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --format, -f FORMAT [FORMAT ...]
                        junit, xray, testrail (default all)
  --test-key TEST_KEY   Xray: existing Jira test issue key (else a new Manual test is described)
  --project-key PROJECT_KEY
                        Xray: Jira project key for a new test
  --case-id CASE_ID     TestRail: case id (e.g. C123) for every row

usage: tirai scan-pii [-h] [--rules RULES [RULES ...]] [--pattern PATTERN] [--keep KEEP]
                      [--every EVERY] [--lang LANG] [--fix]
                      [dir]

positional arguments:
  dir                   evidence folder or a video file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --rules RULES [RULES ...]
                        email, phone, card, token (default all)
  --pattern PATTERN     extra regex (repeatable)
  --keep KEEP           exact text allowed to stay visible (repeatable)
  --every EVERY         seconds between sampled frames
  --lang LANG           tesseract language(s), e.g. eng+vie
  --fix                 blur every hit in the video and refresh the manifest

positional arguments:

positional arguments:
  dir

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --key KEY    SSH private key (default $TIRAI_SIGN_KEY)
  --tsa [TSA]  add an RFC 3161 timestamp (default TSA freetsa.org, or give a URL)

usage: tirai verify [-h] [--out OUT] [--pubkey PUBKEY] [--allowed-signers ALLOWED_SIGNERS]
                    [--identity IDENTITY] [--tsa-ca TSA_CA]
                    [dir]

positional arguments:
  dir

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out OUT             same as DIR (the --out folder used with run/record)
  --pubkey PUBKEY       trusted SSH public key the manifest must be signed with
  --allowed-signers ALLOWED_SIGNERS
                        ssh allowed_signers file (with --identity)
  --identity IDENTITY   signer identity in the allowed_signers file
  --tsa-ca TSA_CA       TSA CA certificate to verify the timestamp chain

positional arguments:
  trace                trace.json or the folder that holds it

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit

positional arguments:
  url

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

                        default: agent-browser when installed
  --timeout TIMEOUT     agent-browser: stop after this many seconds
  --purpose PURPOSE     what the flow proves; becomes the scenario name
  --trace-dir TRACE_DIR
                        bsk: where bsk writes trace.json (default: trace/)
  -o, --output OUTPUT   scenario file to write
  --no-resolve          skip the replay that resolves CSS selectors
  --scope SCOPE         bsk scope for the resolving replay

usage: tirai dbx [-h] [--port PORT] [--detach]

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --port PORT
  --detach, -d  run in the background (log: ~/.tirai/dbx.log)

usage: tirai dbx-connect [-h] [--dsn-env DSN_ENV] --name NAME [--url URL] [--db-host DB_HOST]
                         [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV] [--no-test]
                         [dsn]

positional arguments:
  dsn                   postgresql://user:pw@host:port/db (prefer --dsn-env to keep it out of
                        shell history)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dsn-env DSN_ENV     read the DSN from this environment variable, e.g. EV_DB_DSN
  --name NAME           connection name shown in DBX
  --url URL             DBX web URL
  --db-host DB_HOST     database host as DBX sees it (e.g. a Docker service name)
  --password-env PASSWORD_ENV
                        env var holding the DBX web password
  --no-test             save without asking DBX to test the connection

  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

## Source: docs/getting-started.md

# Getting started

## 1. Install

```bash
# macOS / Linux
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2tsoftwareapp/TIRAI/main/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2tsoftwareapp/TIRAI/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

The installer works on any machine, with or without Python:

| Method | When | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Prebuilt binary** (default when available) | a GitHub Release has `tirai-<os>-<arch>` for this machine | downloads it to `~/.tirai/bin`, verifies `.sha256`; no Python needed |
| **From source** (fallback, or `--source`) | no binary for this machine | Python ≥ 3.10 on the machine → `~/.tirai/venv`; otherwise it downloads [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and a private Python 3.12 into `~/.tirai` (system Python is never touched) |

Force a method with `sh install.sh --binary|--source` (PowerShell: `./install.ps1 --binary|--source`) or
`TIRAI_INSTALL_MODE`. Re-running the installer keeps an installed `tirai` of the same version (`TIRAI_FORCE=1`
reinstalls). `tirai` is linked into `~/.local/bin`, then `tirai setup` reuses what is already on the machine and
installs only what is missing:

| Tool | How | Where |
|---|---|---|
| ffmpeg ≥ 6.0 | any ffmpeg ≥ 6.0 on PATH or in Homebrew/Linuxbrew/snap dirs is used; otherwise a static [BtbN](https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds) 8.1 build (Linux, Windows) or `brew install ffmpeg` (macOS). ffmpeg 4.4 breaks agent-browser recording | `~/.tirai/bin` |
| [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) | kept if on PATH / `~/.local/bin`; else release binary. Chrome for Testing only if `agent-browser doctor` finds none; Linux libraries (`--with-deps`, sudo) only if Chrome fails to start | `~/.tirai/bin` |
| [DBX web](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx) | kept if a DBX web answers on `DBX_URL` / port 4224, `dbx-web` is on PATH, or a `t8y2/dbx` container/image exists; else `browser-static` release package, SHA-256 checked (Linux x64/arm64, Windows x64), Docker image elsewhere | `~/.tirai/dbx` |
| BrowserSkill CLI | kept if installed; offered only when agent-browser is missing or with `tirai setup --only browserskill` | `~/.local/bin` |

Skip any of them with `--skip ffmpeg,agent-browser,dbx,browserskill,skills`. Then:

```bash
tirai doctor
tirai dbx -d          # DBX web on http://127.0.0.1:4224; set DBX_PASSWORD for the web login
```

## Browser drivers

| | `agent-browser` (default) | `bsk` |
|---|---|---|
| Browser | Chrome for Testing, headless (`--headed` to watch) | your real Chrome/Edge via the BrowserSkill extension |
| Recording | 30 fps, animated cursor (`TIRAI_CURSOR=0` to hide) | ~12 fps |
| Extension needed | no | yes |
| `tirai capture` | yes (close the window to finish) | yes (`bsk record`) |

Pick one with `driver:` in the scenario, `--driver`, or `TIRAI_DRIVER`. Both record the active tab only, so TIRAI
records one segment per tab block and composes them.

### Build the binary yourself

```bash
python scripts/build_binary.py             # dist/tirai-<os>-<arch>[.exe] + .sha256 (PyInstaller, one file)
TIRAI_BINARY=dist/tirai-linux-x64 sh install.sh --binary
```

Run it on each OS/arch you ship and attach the files to a GitHub Release; the installers pick them up from
`releases/latest` (or `TIRAI_VERSION=<tag>`).

## 2. Run the demo

```bash
cd examples/demo
docker compose up -d                       # app :8080, PostgreSQL :5432, DBX :4224
cp .env.example .env                       # Windows: copy .env.example .env
```

In DBX (http://127.0.0.1:4224, password `dbx_demo_pw`) create one PostgreSQL connection:
host `db`, port `5432`, database `shop`, user `evidence_ro`, password `ro_demo_pw`. DBX keeps it in its data dir.

```bash
tirai run login-lock.yaml --dry-run        # loads .env next to the scenario; 6 steps, no video
tirai record login-lock.yaml               # evidence/record/final.mp4 + report.md
```

## 3. Your own scenario

```bash
tirai init scenarios/my-feature.yaml
tirai validate scenarios/my-feature.yaml
```

Write steps as *action + expect*, see [scenario format](scenario-format.md) and [annotations](annotations.md).

---

## Source: docs/scenario-format.md

# Scenario reference

```yaml
name: "Login validation + DB verification"   # title card + report heading
tabs:                                         # first tab opens a fresh bsk session, others open as new tabs
  app: { url: "${APP_URL}", label: "WEB APP" }
  db:
    url: "${DBX_URL}"
    label: "DATABASE (DBX)"
    kind: dbx                                 # enables `sql:`
    setup:                                    # runs before recording starts
      - dbx_login: "${DBX_PASSWORD}"
databases:                                    # used by `expect: db`
  default: { dsn: "${EV_DB_DSN}" }            # postgresql:// | mysql:// | sqlite:///path
steps: [...]
```

## Step fields

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Unique step id (`S1`, `S2`, ...) |
| `tab` | yes | Tab name from `tabs:` (a tab with `popup: true` follows a window the page opened) |
| `title` | yes | Header bar text and report row |
| `subtitle` | no | Burned-in subtitle (defaults to `title`); a `{en: ..., vi: ...}` map for several languages |
| `actions` | no | Executed in order |
| `expect` | yes | All must pass for the step to pass (optional when an action is an inline `expect:`) |
| `annotate` | no | Drawn after expectations are checked |
| `hold` | no | Seconds the step stays on screen (default 2.5 recorded, 0.3 dry-run) |
| `zoom` | no | Selector (or `{target, factor, at}`) the video eases in on during this step |
| `layout` | no | `split`: show the previous step (or `split_with: <id>`) beside this one |
| `once` | no | With `cases:`/`matrix:`, run this step only for the first case (`once: last`: only after the last case) |
| `for_each` | no | Repeat this step once per item of a list (or the name of a list in `vars:`/the case); see [Loops](#loops-and-steps-that-run-once) |
| `save` | no | `{ name, selector, attribute?, pattern? }` (or a list): store a value after the actions, before `expect` |
| `writes` | no | `true` or a short text (`creates an order`): this step changes data; see [Steps that write data](#steps-that-write-data) |
| `include` | — | Instead of a step: `include: file.yaml` (+ `with:` vars, `prefix:` for ids) |

## Targets (`@name`)

Name each element once under `targets:` and use `@name` wherever a selector goes: actions, `expect`,
`annotate`, `zoom` and `privacy.selectors`. Each target lists locators tried in order. The first one that
matches **exactly one** element (visible elements win over hidden ones) is tagged in the page with
`data-tirai-id`, and the step addresses it through that attribute.

```yaml
targets:
  email: "#email"                          # the site's own id/test id when it has one
  password: label=Password
  submit:                                  # fallbacks, tried top to bottom
    - testid=login-submit
    - "#submit"
    - role=button[name="Sign in"]
  bob_row: { any: ["text*=bob@demo.local"], within: "#users", nth: 0 }
steps:
  - id: S1
    tab: app
    title: Log in
    actions:
      - fill: { selector: "@email", value: "${EMAIL}" }
      - click: "@submit"
    expect:
      - visible: "@bob_row"
    annotate:
      - box: "@submit"
```

| Locator | Matches |
|---|---|
| `#id`, `.class`, any CSS (or `css=…`) | `document.querySelectorAll` |
| `testid=x` | `data-testid`, `data-test-id`, `data-test`, `data-qa`, `data-cy` equal to `x` |
| `role=button[name="Save"]` | role (`textbox`, `button`, `link`, `combobox`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `heading`, `tab`, `menuitem`, `option`, `cell`, `row`, `dialog`, `img`, or any ARIA role) + exact accessible name; `role=dialog` alone = any |
| `label=Email` | form field whose label (`<label>`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) is exactly `Email` |
| `placeholder=Search` | element with that placeholder |
| `text=Total` / `text*=Total` | innermost element whose text equals / contains the value |

- `within: <css>` limits the search to one container; `nth: <n>` picks the n-th match (0-based) on purpose.
- A locator can also be written inline: `click: role=button[name="Sign in"]` works without a `targets:` entry.
- **No guessing:** 0 or 2+ matches for every locator fails the step and lists what each locator matched,
  for example `target @save: no locator matched exactly one element (role=button[name="Save"]: 2 [button in form#a, button in form#b])`.
- **Fallback used:** when an earlier locator stops matching and a later one finds the element, the step still
  passes, prints `warning: target @submit: #submit: 0 -> used 'role=button[name="Sign in"]'; update the target`,
  and stores it under `warnings` in `timeline.json`.
- Tags are kept in sync while the page re-renders (SPA) and are re-applied after navigation. The page only gains
  the `data-tirai-id` attribute; nothing visible changes.
- A selector that matches nothing (plain CSS or a target) ends with `; nearby: #email (textbox "Email")`
  suggestions taken from the current page.
- Browser tabs only; desktop (`app:`) tabs keep their agent-desktop selectors.

`tirai inspect <scenario>` dry-runs the flow and, after every step, writes `<out>/inspect/<step>.md` (each
element's role, name and unique locators, preferred first) and one `<out>/inspect/targets.yaml` with a
ready-to-paste `targets:` block for every page reached, including pages after login. It prefers test ids and
stable ids/names, skips ids that look generated, and leaves out elements with no unique locator.
`tirai inspect <url>` does the same for a single page.

## Actions

| Action | Example |
|---|---|
| `navigate` | `navigate: ${APP_URL}` |
| `fill` | `fill: { selector: "#email", value: "a@b.c" }` |
| `click` | `click: "button[type=submit]"` |
| `press` | `press: Enter` or `press: { key: "Ctrl+Enter", selector: ".cm-content" }` |
| `wait` | `wait: 500` (ms) |
| `wait_for` | `wait_for: "#welcome"`, `wait_for: { selector: "#menu [role=treeitem]", timeout: 15000 }`, or `wait_for: { idle: true, timeout: 15000 }` (document loaded and no new request for 1 s; warns and continues on timeout) |
| `sql` | `sql: "SELECT ..."` (DBX tab: opens a query editor once, types, runs with Ctrl+Enter) |
| `dbx_login` | `dbx_login: "${DBX_PASSWORD}"` (tab `setup:` only; skipped if already logged in) |
| `select` | `select: { selector: "#country", value: VN }` (option `value`; a list for multi-select) |
| `hover` | `hover: "#menu"` |
| `scroll` | `scroll: "#footer"` (scrolls the element into view) |
| `upload` | `upload: { selector: "input[type=file]", file: fixtures/invoice.pdf }` (path relative to the scenario; a list for several files) |
| `eval` | `eval: "localStorage.setItem('token', '${TOKEN}')"` — run JS in the page (seed cookies/localStorage, flags); fails if it throws or returns `false`; prefer real actions for anything the video should show |
| `dialog` | `dialog: accept` or `dialog: dismiss` — put it before the action that opens `alert`/`confirm`/`prompt`; lasts until the page navigates |
| `clear` | `clear: "#date"` — select-all + Backspace; clears masked inputs (date pickers) that keep their value on `fill: ""` |
| `download` | `download: { selector: "button#print", path: report.pdf, append: true }` (agent-browser only) — clicks the element, waits for the file and keeps it in `<out>/downloads/`; the file's own `download` name is used when `path` is omitted; `append: true` adds the PDF's pages to the end of `final.mp4` |
| `expect` | `expect: { value: { selector: "#ctrl", equals: X9 } }` (or a list) — a check between actions, e.g. before a tab switch unmounts the field; a failure stops the step |

Before `click`, `fill`, `select`, `hover`, `upload` and `press` (with a selector), TIRAI scrolls the element into
view when it is outside the viewport (`settings.auto_scroll: false` turns it off).

Selectors are CSS (native `:has()` works, e.g. `button:has(svg.add)`) or the locators under
[Targets](#targets-name). Playwright-only syntax (`:has-text()`, `:text-is()`, `>>`, `:visible`) never matches in
agent-browser/bsk, so `tirai validate` rejects it and suggests a locator. A CSS list (`"a, b"`) takes the first
match in page order, not list order; `validate` warns and suggests `targets:` fallbacks.

## Expectations

| Expect | Example |
|---|---|
| `visible` | `visible: "#email"` |
| `text_contains` | `text_contains: { selector: ".error", text: "locked" }` (no selector = whole page) |
| `not_visible` | `not_visible: "#login-error"` (missing, zero-size, `display:none` or `visibility:hidden`) |
| `text_matches` | `text_matches: { selector: "#total", pattern: "^\\d+ items$", flags: i }` (JavaScript RegExp, like `save.pattern`) |
| `url_contains` | `url_contains: "/dashboard"` |
| `value` | `value: { selector: "#email", equals: "a@b.c" }` (form field value) |
| `attribute` | `attribute: { selector: "#save", name: disabled, equals: "" }` |
| `count` | `count: { selector: "table tbody tr", equals: 3 }` |
| `request` | `request: { url_contains: "/api/orders", status: 201 }` (any page or XHR/fetch request seen by the page; `status` optional) |
| `no_console_errors` | `no_console_errors: {}` or `{ ignore: ["favicon"] }` (console errors/exceptions raised during this step) |
| `pdf` | `pdf: { path: report.pdf, pages: 2, contains: "Total", annotate: [{ arrow: { text: "27,000", label: "OK", from: top } }], zoom: true }` — checks the downloaded PDF; `annotate:` (`true`/`auto` or `box`/`arrow`/`highlight`/`circle`/`badge` by `text:` or `{x,y,w,h}`) draws Snagit-style callouts on the preview pages appended to `final.mp4` |
| `xlsx` | `xlsx: { path: report.xlsx, sheets: [Orders], contains: "A-1", annotate: [{ box: { cell: "C2", label: "Matched" } }], preview: true }` — checks sheet names/cell text and optionally appends an annotated sheet preview |
| `image` | `image: { path: shot.png, contains: "OK", annotate: [{ box: { text: "OK" } }], preview: true }` — checks an image (optional OCR `contains`) and appends an annotated preview (by `{x,y,w,h}` or OCR `text:`) |
| `db` | `db: { sql: "SELECT status FROM users WHERE id=2", rows: [{status: LOCKED}] }` (`columns:` defaults to the keys of the first expected row, in SELECT order) — numbers compare by value, so `204000` matches `"204000.00000"` from PostgreSQL `numeric` |

DOM checks retry for up to 6 s (`settings.expect_timeout: 15` for slow SPAs). `db` runs read-only against `databases.<name>.dsn` (default `default`),
independently of what the DBX tab shows: DBX draws its result grid on a canvas, so its cells are not DOM text.

Every step also notes failed requests (HTTP 4xx/5xx seen by the page, e.g. a silent `401` from an expired
session) and console errors raised while it ran. They are printed, stored in `timeline.json` and listed in the
report even when the step passes. `settings.strict_network: true` fails the step instead;
`settings.ignore_requests: ["/healthz"]` drops URLs you expect to fail.

## Steps that write data

A dry-run runs the real actions (it only skips the video), so a step that saves an order creates one every time.
Mark such steps with `writes:`; `sql:` actions with `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/DDL count automatically.

```yaml
steps:
  - id: SAVE
    tab: app
    title: Save the order
    writes: creates an order (受注)
    actions: [{ click: "@save" }]
    save: { name: orderNo, selector: "#orderNo" }
    expect: [{ text_contains: { text: "saved" } }]
cleanup:                                   # after the run; not recorded; only when a write step ran
  - tab: db
    actions:
      - sql: "DELETE FROM orders WHERE order_no = '{{orderNo}}'"
```

- `tirai validate` lists the steps that write data.
- `tirai run --dry-run` stops before the first write step and reports the steps before it; `--allow-writes` runs
  everything. `tirai record` dry-runs up to the first write step, then records the whole flow once.
- `--until <step>` stops a dry-run after that step (or the last step expanded from it).
- The report has a "Data written" table with each write step and the values it saved, so test data can be
  cleaned up by hand when there is no `cleanup:`.

## Iterating on a long flow

```bash
tirai run flow.yaml --dry-run --keep-session            # prints: session kept: tirai-1234
tirai run flow.yaml --dry-run --session tirai-1234 --from-step S14
```

`--from-step` continues on the pages the kept session has open (no new tab, no tab `setup:`), with the values
saved by the previous run in the same `--out` folder. `--fresh` clears cookies and storage before tab setup, so
the run starts logged out instead of reusing an old session (bsk cannot clear HttpOnly cookies).

## Popup windows

```yaml
tabs:
  app: { url: "${APP_URL}" }
  order: { popup: true, match: "/AB03001" }   # adopted when a step first uses it
```

A `popup: true` tab has no URL: the first step on it binds to the newest browser tab the page opened
(`window.open`, `target=_blank`) whose URL contains `match`, waiting up to `expect_timeout`. If that window
closes and a new one opens, the next step binds again.

## Viewport

`settings.viewport: { width: 1600, height: 900 }` sets the page size on agent-browser (each tab and popup).
bsk uses the size of your browser window.

## Recording model

BrowserSkill records one tab at a time (max 10 min per recording, no audio). TIRAI starts a new
segment whenever the active tab changes, stores per-step start/end offsets in `timeline.json`, and
`tirai compose` cuts each step out of its segment and joins them in scenario order.

## Data-driven scenarios

```yaml
vars: { base: "${APP_URL}" }                  # scenario-wide values for {{name}}
cases:                                        # or matrix: {browser: [a, b], locale: [en, vi]} (cartesian product)
  - { name: Alice, email: alice@demo.local, status: ACTIVE }
  - { name: Bob,   email: bob@demo.local,   status: LOCKED }
steps:
  - id: OPEN
    once: true                                # first case only
    tab: app
    title: App is reachable
    actions: [{ navigate: "{{base}}" }]
    expect: [{ visible: "#email" }]
  - include: common/login.yaml                # list of steps, or a mapping with steps:
    with: { password_env: APP_PASSWORD }
  - id: DB
    tab: app
    title: "DB status is {{status}} (screen said: {{message}})"
    expect:
      - db:
          sql: "SELECT status FROM users WHERE email = '{{email}}'"
          rows: [{ status: "{{status}}" }]
          save: { db_status: status }         # column -> variable for later steps
```

- `{{name}}` comes from `vars:`, the current case, or a value saved earlier; `${NAME}` stays an environment variable.
- Steps repeat once per case with ids `LOGIN-1`, `LOGIN-2`, … and titles prefixed `[Alice]`.
- `save: { name, selector, attribute?, pattern?, flags?, timeout?, allow_empty? }` stores an element's
  value/text (first group of the JavaScript RegExp `pattern` if it has one), as an action or as a step key. It
  polls until the value is non-empty and matches (up to `timeout` seconds, default `expect_timeout`), so async
  forms need no `eval:` poll; `allow_empty: true` stores empty values. Values saved in one action are visible
  to the next action or check of the same step. `db: { save: { variable: column } }` stores a column of the first
  row; a missing column or an empty result is an error.

### Loops and steps that run once

```yaml
vars:
  lines: [{ code: A01, qty: 2 }, { code: B07, qty: 1 }]
steps:
  - id: LINE
    for_each: lines                           # or an inline list; scalars are {{item}} (rename with as:)
    tab: app
    title: "Line {{index}}: {{code}}"
    actions:
      - click: "@add_row"
      - fill: { selector: "#lines tr:last-child .code", value: "{{code}}" }
    expect: [{ value: { selector: "#lines tr:last-child .code", equals: "{{code}}" } }]
  - id: SAVE                                  # runs once, after every line
    ...
```

`for_each` repeats one step per item (`LINE-1`, `LINE-2`, …; `{{index}}` counts from 1). With `cases:`, use
`once: last` for a step that must run once after the last case (`once: true` = first case only).
- A placeholder that is the whole value keeps its type (`equals: "{{count}}"` stays a number). An undefined
  variable at run time is an error.

## Video options

| Option | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Chapters | automatic | `final.mp4` has one chapter per step (title card included) |
| `zoom: "#email"` | step | eases in (≈0.6 s) on the element and holds; add `out: true` in `{ target, factor, at, out }` to ease back out |
| `zoom: annotate` / `camera: annotate` | step / `settings:` | automatically zooms in on the `annotate:` union box + labels, holds, and eases back out smoothly |
| `spotlight: true` | step / `settings:` | dims the page around active `annotate:` targets (and on annotated PDF/Excel/image previews) |
| `pace: human` (`slow`) | `settings:` | when recording, glides a 60fps virtual cursor with click ripples, types ASCII fields progressively, and adds brief natural pauses (dry-run stays full speed) |
| `theme:` | top-level / `settings:` | customize `font`, `header_size`, `subtitle_size`, `subtitle_height`, `subtitle_bg`, `subtitle_color`, `tab_colors`, `pass_color`, `fail_color`, `accent`, `cursor_color`, `ripple_color`, `spotlight_opacity` |
| `layout: split` | step | left: last frame of the previous step (or `split_with`), right: this step; useful for UI → DB proof |
| `--lang vi` | `tirai record` / `compose` | burns that subtitle language; every language is also written as `subtitles.<lang>.srt` |
| `zoom: follow` | step | zooms in and pans from one action target (click, fill, select…) to the next |
| `camera: follow` | `settings:` | `zoom: follow` for every step without its own `zoom:`; `camera_factor` (default 1.6) sets the zoom |
| `--trim-still` | `tirai record` / `compose` (or `settings.trim_still: true`) | stretches of 2 s or more where the screen does not change play at 8× with a badge; each step's start and closing `hold` stay at normal speed |
| `fast_forward: 4` | `settings:` | `wait`/`wait_for` longer than 1.5 s play at 4× with a "4x" badge (default 4; `0` turns it off) |
| `single_tab: true` | `settings:` | apps that open child screens with `window.open`/`target=_blank` navigate the same tab, so the screencast never freezes on the opener page (agent-browser; declare `popup: true` tabs instead when you need both pages) |
| `--voice` | `tirai compose` | reads each subtitle aloud (macOS `say`, Windows SAPI, Linux `espeak-ng`, or `$TIRAI_TTS_CMD` with `{text}` `{out}` `{lang}`); a clip is held until its speech ends |

## Desktop apps (agent-desktop)

A tab with `app:` instead of `url:` drives a native app through the OS accessibility tree
([agent-desktop](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop): macOS AX, Windows UI Automation, Linux AT-SPI) and
records the screen around its window with ffmpeg. Browser and desktop tabs can be mixed in one scenario.

```yaml
tabs:
  calc: { app: gnome-calculator, label: Calculator }   # name: overrides the name used to find the app
steps:
  - id: S1
    tab: calc
    title: 7 + 8 = 15
    actions:
      - click: "button:7"                              # role:name (exact name) or a bare accessible name
      - click: "button:+"
      - click: "button:8"
      - click: "button:="
    expect:
      - text_contains: { selector: { role: textfield }, text: "15" }   # mapping = agent-desktop find filters
```

Actions: `click`, `fill` (set-value, falls back to clear + type), `press`, `select`, `hover`, `scroll`, `wait`,
`wait_for`. Expectations: `visible`, `not_visible`, `text_contains`, `text_matches`, `value`. `annotate:` and
`privacy:` masking are browser-only (use `privacy.ocr` to scan the final video). Install with
`tirai setup --only agent-desktop`. Needs: Linux X11 with AT-SPI (agent-desktop supports Ubuntu 24.04+) and a
window manager; macOS Accessibility + Screen Recording permission for the terminal; Windows desktop session.

## Subtitles in several languages

```yaml
lang: en                                      # default burned language (override with --lang)
steps:
  - id: S2
    subtitle:
      en: "Step 2: malformed email -> validation error"
      vi: "Bước 2: email sai định dạng -> báo lỗi"
```

Missing languages fall back to the first one given for that step.

## Privacy: automatic PII masking

```yaml
privacy:
  mask: [email, phone, card, token]           # built-in rules
  patterns: ['ACC-\d{6}']                     # extra regexes (JavaScript syntax)
  selectors: [".api-key"]                     # always covered
  keep: ["bob@demo.local"]                    # exact strings that stay visible (e.g. the record under test)
  inputs: true                                # also cover matching input/textarea values (default)
```

Matches are covered with an opaque box in the page (so screenshots and video both hide them) and stay covered
while the DOM changes. With agent-browser the mask is registered as a page init script, so it is active before the page's own scripts on every load; it is also re-applied after every navigation, click and action. Set `privacy: false` on a
tab to skip it. Limitations: text drawn on a canvas (e.g. DBX result cells) is not scanned — cover those with an
`annotate: blur` grid target, or let the OCR pass below catch them — and values in step titles, subtitles or
`save`d variables are not rewritten.

### OCR pass over the final video

```yaml
privacy:
  mask: [email, phone]
  ocr: fix          # off (default) | warn | fix (pixelate hits and rewrite final.mp4) | fail (exit non-zero)
```

After composing, frames are sampled (1/s) and read with tesseract (`tirai setup --only ocr`), so text drawn on a
canvas (DBX grids, images, desktop apps) is checked against the same rules; `keep:` still applies. Hits are
reported masked with time and box. On demand: `tirai scan-pii evidence/record [--rules email phone] [--fix]`.
OCR can misread UI text as an email-like string, so review `warn` hits before relying on them.

---

## Source: docs/annotations.md

# Annotations reference

`annotate.js` renders inside a shadow root (`position:fixed`, `pointer-events:none`, max z-index),
so it never changes how the page behaves. It is re-injected on every step; each step starts clean.

| Shape | Scenario form | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `box` | `box: { target: "#email", label: "Email" }` | rounded rectangle |
| `circle` | `circle: { target: ".error" }` | ellipse around target |
| `arrow` | `arrow: { target: ".error", from: right, label: "Error", length: 110 }` | `from`: left, right, top, bottom, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right |
| `text` | `text: { target: "#total", label: "Sum is wrong" }` | floating label |
| `badge` | `badge: { target: "#save", n: 1 }` | numbered marker |
| `highlight` | `highlight: { target: ".row-2" }` | translucent marker fill (yellow) |
| `blur` | `blur: { target: "#password" }` | masks sensitive content; always instant |

Common options: `color` (`#e5252a`), `width` (3), `padding` (6), `label`, `labelPos`
(right, left, top, bottom), `anim`, `duration`, `id`.

## Targets

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| CSS selector | `"#email"` (first visible match) |
| Visible text | `{ text: "Sign in", within: "form", exact: true, nth: 0 }` |
| Viewport rect | `{ x: 100, y: 200, w: 300, h: 40 }` |
| Relative to element | `{ selector: "canvas", rel: { x: 0, y: 26, w: 120, h: 26 } }` |
| Canvas data grid (DBX) | `{ grid: { column: status, toColumn: failed_logins, row: 1 } }` |

Grid targets take x/width from DOM header cells (`.data-grid-header-cell`) and y from the canvas body
(`canvas.canvas-grid-surface`, 26 px rows); override with `header`, `body`, `rowHeight`.

A missing target throws, so the step fails instead of silently recording a wrong frame.

## Animation

| `anim` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `draw` (default) | strokes draw on once (~0.4 s), arrow grows tail to tip, highlight wipes left to right, label fades in last |
| `fade` | fade in ~0.2 s |
| `none` | appears instantly (strict evidence) |

No looping or pulsing: BrowserSkill records at roughly 12 fps, so repeated motion looks jerky.
Removing annotations fades them out in 0.16 s. Set a default for a page with `__ann.config({ anim: "none" })`.

---

## Source: docs/configuration.md

# Configuration

Nothing is tied to one OS or install location. Every external tool, font and timing value can be overridden.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `TIRAI_HOME` | `~/.tirai` | where setup puts ffmpeg, agent-browser (`bin/`) and DBX web (`dbx/`) |
| `TIRAI_DRIVER` | `agent-browser` if installed, else `bsk` | browser driver (scenario `driver:` and `--driver` win) |
| `TIRAI_HEADED` | off | show the agent-browser window (same as `--headed`) |
| `TIRAI_CURSOR` | `1` | draw agent-browser's animated cursor in recordings |
| `TIRAI_SIGN_KEY` | unset | SSH private key; `compose` re-signs `manifest.sha256` with it after rebuilding |
| `TIRAI_TTS_CMD` | unset | custom voice command for `--voice`, e.g. `piper --output_file {out}` (`{text}`, `{out}`, `{lang}`) |
| `AGENT_DESKTOP_BIN` / `AGENT_BROWSER_BIN` | PATH, `~/.tirai/bin` | explicit driver binaries |
| `TIRAI_AGENT_BROWSER_VERSION` | `0.43.0` | agent-browser release `tirai setup` downloads (pinned digest only for the default) |
| `TIRAI_DBX_VERSION` | `0.6.72` | DBX web release `tirai setup` downloads |
| `TIRAI_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED` | unset | `1` accepts a setup download whose SHA-256 is unknown |
| `AGENT_BROWSER_BIN` | `~/.tirai/bin`, PATH, `~/.local/bin` | agent-browser CLI |
| `DBX_WEB_BIN`, `DBX_WEB_DIR` | `~/.tirai/dbx` | DBX web server binary / package folder |
| `DBX_PORT`, `DBX_DATA_DIR`, `DBX_PASSWORD` | `4224`, `~/.tirai/dbx-data`, none | passed to DBX web by `tirai dbx` |
| `BSK_BIN` | `bsk` on PATH, then `$BSK_INSTALL_DIR`, `~/.local/bin` | BrowserSkill CLI |
| `FFMPEG_BIN`, `FFPROBE_BIN` | `~/.tirai/bin`, PATH, then Homebrew / winget / choco / scoop locations | ffmpeg tools (≥ 6.0) |
| `TIRAI_FONT`, `TIRAI_FONT_BOLD` | DejaVu Sans (Linux, also via `fc-match`), Arial Unicode/Arial (macOS), Arial/Segoe UI (Windows) | title, header and subtitle font files |
| `TIRAI_SUBTITLE_FONT` | family of the font above | font family name for burned subtitles |
| `TIRAI_VIDEO_SIZE` | size of the largest recorded segment | output content size, e.g. `1920x1080` |
| `TIRAI_TIMING_SCALE` | `1.0` | multiply all settle delays (use `2` on slow machines) |
| `TIRAI_EXPECT_TIMEOUT` | `6` | seconds DOM expectations retry |

Installer variables (`install.sh` / `install.ps1`): `TIRAI_REPO`, `TIRAI_REF`, `TIRAI_SOURCE` (local checkout
or archive URL), `TIRAI_HOME` (`~/.tirai`), `TIRAI_BIN_DIR` (`~/.local/bin`), `TIRAI_EXTRAS` (`postgres`),
`TIRAI_NO_SETUP=1`, `TIRAI_SETUP_ARGS` (Windows, when piping into `iex`).

## Scenario variables and `.env`

`${VAR}` placeholders are read from the environment. `tirai validate|run|record` also load a `.env`
file next to the scenario (or `--env-file <path>`); variables already set in the shell win.
This works the same in bash, zsh, PowerShell and cmd.

## Scenario `settings:`

```yaml
settings:
  hold: 2.5            # seconds each recorded step stays on screen
  timing_scale: 1.0    # same as TIRAI_TIMING_SCALE (env wins)
  expect_timeout: 6    # same as TIRAI_EXPECT_TIMEOUT (env wins)
  camera: follow       # zoom + pan to each action target (or per step: zoom: follow)
  camera_factor: 1.6
  fast_forward: 4      # speed of long waits in the video; 0 = real time
```

## DBX tab overrides

```yaml
tabs:
  db:
    url: ${DBX_URL}
    kind: dbx
    dbx:
      new_query: "New Query"           # button text that opens a SQL editor (change for a localized UI)
      editor: ".cm-content"            # SQL editor element
      password: "input[type=password]" # DBX login field
      run_key: "Ctrl+Enter"            # default: Meta+Enter on macOS, Ctrl+Enter elsewhere
      connection: shop-readonly        # connection the query editor uses (default: connect.name); needed when DBX has several
      connect:                         # optional: create/update the DBX connection before the tab opens
        name: shop-readonly            # connection name in DBX
        database: default              # key in `databases:` whose DSN is used (default: default)
        host: evpg                     # DB host as DBX sees it (e.g. Docker service); default: the DSN host
        password_env: DBX_PASSWORD     # env var with the DBX web password (default: DBX_PASSWORD)
```

`tirai dbx-connect --dsn-env EV_DB_DSN --name shop-readonly [--db-host evpg] [--url ...]` does the same from the
command line. DBX is asked to test the connection first; use a read-only database user.

## Skill locations

`tirai install-skill --agent <name>` and `tirai setup` use the paths in [agents.md](agents.md);
`--project <dir>` installs into a repository, `--dest <dir>` into any directory.

---

## Source: docs/agents.md

# Installing the skill for an agent

The skill is `skills/tirai-evidence/` (SKILL.md + references). Every agent uses the same `tirai` and `bsk` CLIs.

| Agent | Install | Skill location |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add 2tsoftwareapp/TIRAI` then `/plugin install tirai-evidence@tirai`, or `tirai install-skill --agent claude` | `~/.claude/skills` or `<project>/.claude/skills` |
| Codex | `tirai install-skill --agent codex` | `~/.agents/skills` or `<project>/.agents/skills` |
| Antigravity | `tirai install-skill --agent antigravity` | `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills` or `<project>/.agent/skills` |
| Cursor | `tirai install-skill --agent cursor` | `~/.cursor/skills` or `<project>/.cursor/skills` |
| Devin | `tirai install-skill --agent devin --project .` and commit it | `<repo>/.agents/skills` |
| Other | `tirai install-skill --agent claude --dest <skills dir>` | any directory the agent scans |

`tirai setup` installs the skill for every agent it detects (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini/antigravity`,
`~/.cursor`); Devin skills are per repository, so use `--project`.

Add `--project <dir>` to install into a repository instead of the user profile, `--force` to overwrite.
Also install BrowserSkill's own skill so the agent can explore pages: `bsk install-skill --harness <id>`.

Agents without skill support can read `AGENTS.md` / `skills/tirai-evidence/SKILL.md` directly.

## MCP server

MCP-capable agents can call TIRAI as tools instead of the shell:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "tirai": { "command": "tirai", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

Tools: `doctor`, `init`, `validate`, `dry_run`, `record`, `compose`, `verify`, `from_trace`, `annotate_js`. Each
accepts an optional `cwd`; results are the CLI output, with `isError` set when the command fails.

## Capture a flow instead of writing it

```bash
tirai capture http://127.0.0.1:8080/ --purpose "Locked account is rejected" -o scenarios/locked.yaml
```

A browser window opens (agent-browser); click through the flow, then close the window. Selectors come from the
page (id, data-testid, name, aria-label, else a short path); passwords become `${ENV}` placeholders.
`--driver bsk` uses BrowserSkill's Agent Window (`bsk record`) instead.
TIRAI replays the trace to resolve every target to a CSS selector, splits it into steps at each click/navigation
and derives an expectation from what changed (new URL or new text). Redacted values such as passwords become
`${PASSWORD}`-style placeholders. Review titles and expectations, add `annotate:`, then dry-run.
`tirai from-trace <trace dir> -o file.yaml` converts an existing trace (`--no-resolve` skips the replay and
leaves `TODO role=… name=…` selectors).

---

## Source: docs/architecture.md

# Architecture

```text
scenario.yaml ──► tirai validate
      │
      ▼
tirai run --dry-run ──► agent-browser | BrowserSkill (bsk) ──► real Chrome/Edge tabs (app, DBX web)
      │                    │  fill / click / press / evaluate
      │                    └─ annotate.js injected per step (boxes, arrows, labels, blur)
      ▼
tirai run --record ──► driver recording per contiguous tab block ──► seg-NN-<tab>.mp4 + timeline.json
      │                                               └──► expect: db (read-only driver)
      ▼
tirai compose ──► ffmpeg: cut steps, header bar, title card, concat, burn subtitles
      └──► final.mp4, subtitles.srt, report.md/.html/.xlsx, timeline.final.json, manifest.sha256
```

| Component | Owner | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Browser control, screenshots, MP4 (default) | [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) | single binary, no extension, headless or headed, 30 fps |
| Browser control in your own browser | [Tencent BrowserSkill](https://github.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill) | real logged-in browser; also powers `tirai capture` |
| Database UI in the browser | [DBX web](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx) | many database engines, password-protected web UI |
| Scenario, checks, annotations, timeline, composition | TIRAI | the evidence-specific parts |

Design rules:

- **Dry-run before record**: recording only happens for a scenario that already passes, so videos have no failed attempts.
- **Per-tab segments**: both drivers record a single tab, so the runner starts a new segment on every tab switch and composition restores scenario order.
- **Checks are independent of pixels**: DOM checks read the page; DB checks query read-only, because DBX renders result cells on a canvas.
- **Fail closed**: a missing selector, annotation target or env var fails the step.

The previous spec-to-test platform (TypeScript workspaces) is preserved on branch `archive/tirai-v1`.

---

## Source: docs/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `ffmpeg write failed: Broken pipe` when agent-browser stops recording | ffmpeg too old (4.4 fails); run `tirai setup` to get a current build in `~/.tirai/bin` |
| `tirai doctor` says ffmpeg too old | `tirai setup` installs a newer one; or point `FFMPEG_BIN` at ffmpeg ≥ 6.0 |
| DBX releases unreachable during setup | setup falls back to the Docker image; rerun later or set `DBX_WEB_BIN` |
| `bsk doctor` shows no extension | open the browser with the BrowserSkill extension enabled and connected |
| `bsk open failed ... session <id> unknown` | TIRAI closes the stale session and retries once; if it persists: `bsk session list`, `bsk close --session <id>`, or `--scope <new>` |
| `requires an unused strict observation` / `control context no longer belongs` | page changed under an action; add `wait_for` before the next action. The runner already syncs before every action |
| `annotate: target not found` | selector not visible at annotation time; check `step-<id>.png` from the dry-run |
| DBX cells not found by text | DBX draws results on a canvas: use `{ grid: { column, row } }` targets and `expect: db` |
| `tirai: command not found` after install | open a new terminal (PATH was updated) or run `~/.local/bin/tirai` / `%USERPROFILE%\\.local\\bin\\tirai.cmd` |
| ffmpeg installed by winget but not found | open a new terminal, or set `FFMPEG_BIN`; TIRAI also checks `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Microsoft\\WinGet\\Links` |
| Linux package install asks for a sudo password | run the printed `sudo ...` command yourself, then `tirai setup` again |
| DBX step fails with "no connection selected" or the grid is missing | DBX has several connections and the editor has none selected; set `tabs.<db>.dbx.connection` (or use `dbx.connect`, whose name is selected) |
| `tirai dbx -d` says port 4224 is used by another service | it starts DBX on the next free port and prints it; set `DBX_URL` (or `--port` / `DBX_PORT`) to that port for scenarios |
| `setup` skips a step with "sudo needs a password" | no terminal for the sudo prompt (agent shell); run the printed command yourself, or rerun `tirai setup` in a terminal |
| DBX query does not run on macOS | the run shortcut defaults to `Meta+Enter`; override with `tabs.<db>.dbx.run_key` |
| Steps flaky on a slow machine | `TIRAI_TIMING_SCALE=2` |
| Subtitles missing Vietnamese glyphs | set `TIRAI_FONT` (and `TIRAI_FONT_BOLD`) to a Unicode .ttf |
| `missing environment variable X` | export it; `tirai validate` lists every variable the scenario needs |
| Video is choppy | BrowserSkill records ~12 fps; keep `anim: draw`/`fade` short or use `anim: none` |

---

## Source: skills/tirai-evidence/SKILL.md

---
name: tirai-evidence
description: Record test evidence videos from a written test scenario. Drives Chrome with vercel-labs agent-browser (default) or Tencent BrowserSkill (bsk), checks the database through DBX web in a second tab, draws Snagit-style boxes/arrows/labels on the page, and composes one MP4 with subtitles and a step report using ffmpeg. Use when the user wants an evidence video, a recorded test run, "quay evidence", or step-by-step proof of a UI + DB behaviour.
---

# TIRAI evidence recording

Workflow: **scenario → dry-run → record → compose**. Never record before the dry-run passes.

## 0. Check the environment (once per machine)

```bash
tirai doctor            # if tirai is missing or a check fails: see references/setup.md
tirai setup --yes       # installs ffmpeg >= 6, agent-browser, DBX web, BrowserSkill CLI, skills
tirai dbx -d            # start DBX web (http://127.0.0.1:4224) when the scenario has a db tab
```

All required checks must be `ok`. Works on macOS, Linux and Windows; follow
[references/setup.md](references/setup.md). The default driver needs no extension; only `driver: bsk` needs the user to install the BrowserSkill extension;
never use `sudo` without asking.

## 1. Write the scenario with the user

Start from `tirai init scenarios/<name>.yaml` and fill it in. One step = one thing to prove:

```yaml
- id: S2
  tab: app                       # which browser tab (declared under tabs:)
  title: Invalid email format
  subtitle: "Step 2: enter a malformed email -> validation error"
  actions:                       # what to do
    - fill: { selector: "#email", value: "alice-at-demo.local" }
    - click: "button[type=submit]"
  expect:                        # what must be true (required)
    - text_contains: { selector: ".error", text: "Email format is invalid." }
  annotate:                      # what to draw once expectations are checked
    - box: { target: "#email" }
    - arrow: { target: ".error", from: right, label: "Validation error" }
```

- Full vocabulary (actions, expect, DB tabs, databases): [references/scenario.md](references/scenario.md).
- Annotation shapes, targets and animation: [references/annotations.md](references/annotations.md).
- Name elements once under `targets:` and use `@name` in actions/expect/annotate/zoom (fallback locators like
  `testid=`, `#id`, `role=button[name="Save"]`, `label=`, `text=`; see [references/scenario.md](references/scenario.md)).
  Get them with `tirai inspect <file>` (or `tirai inspect <url>`): it dry-runs the flow and writes each page's
  elements plus a ready `targets:` block to `evidence/inspect/`, pages after login included; do not guess.
  Or let the user click the flow once: `tirai capture <url> -o <file>` opens a browser; the user clicks the flow
  and closes the window.
- A failure ending in `nearby: …` lists the page's closest elements: fix the target from it. A `warning: target
  @x … used …` means a fallback locator was needed: update that target.
- Database tab: `dbx.connect: {name: ..., host: ...}` on the DBX tab creates the connection from `databases.default`
  (or run `tirai dbx-connect --dsn-env EV_DB_DSN --name <name>`); no manual DBX setup.
- Repeated flows: `include:` shared steps, `cases:`/`matrix:` for data, `for_each:` to repeat one step per item
  (N order lines), `once: last` for a step after the last case, `save:` to reuse on-screen values as `{{name}}`.
- Mark steps that create/change data with `writes: <what>` and undo them under `cleanup:`; a dry-run stops before
  them unless `--allow-writes`. Never dry-run writes repeatedly on a shared tenant without asking the user.
- Popups (`window.open`): declare a tab `{popup: true, match: "/path"}` and use it in the next step.
- Check a field before an action unmounts it with an inline `- expect: {...}` among the actions.
- Slow SPAs: `settings.expect_timeout: 15` or `wait_for: {idle: true}` instead of fixed `wait:`;
  `settings.viewport: {width: 1600, height: 900}` when forms do not fit.
- Selectors are CSS or TIRAI locators; Playwright syntax (`:has-text`, `>>`) does not work. Quote values that start
  with `${...}` or `{{...}}` inside `{ }`.
- Video: `zoom: <selector>` on a step, `layout: split` to show UI and DB side by side; `subtitle: {en, vi}` + `--lang`.
- Real data on screen: add `privacy: { mask: [email, phone, card, token] }` (and `keep:` for the record under test).
- Secrets go in `${ENV_VAR}` only. Put values in a git-ignored `.env` next to the scenario
  (loaded automatically, or pass `--env-file`); never write values into the scenario.
- DB checks must use a **read-only** database user.

Then `tirai validate <file>` and fix every reported problem.

## 2. Dry-run (no video)

```bash
tirai run <file> --dry-run
```

Read the failing step's `expect ... -> actual ...` line and `evidence/dry-run/step-<id>.png`.
Fix the scenario (selector, wait, data) or report the product bug to the user. Repeat until all steps pass.
`network:`/`console:` lines (e.g. a 401) mean the page had errors even if the step passed: check them, and use
`--fresh` to start without an old login.

Long flow: `--keep-session` once, then `--session <name> --from-step <id>` to rerun only the tail; `--until <id>`
stops early.

## 3. Record + compose

```bash
tirai record <file>            # dry-run again, record, then compose
```

Outputs in `evidence/record/`: `final.mp4`, `subtitles.srt`, `report.md`, `report.html`, `report.xlsx`,
`timeline.final.json`, `manifest.sha256`, per-tab `seg-*.mp4` and `step-*.png`. To document a bug, record the
failing run with `tirai record <file> --record-failures` (stops after the first failing step, FAIL in the header).
`--trim-still` fast-forwards long stretches where nothing changes. Re-compose without re-recording: `tirai compose evidence/record/timeline.json`.

Optional extras: `tirai compose evidence/record/timeline.json --voice` (spoken subtitles),
`tirai scan-pii evidence/record --fix` (OCR pass for PII drawn on canvas), `tirai sign evidence/record --key
~/.ssh/id_ed25519 [--tsa]` then `tirai verify evidence/record --pubkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`,
`tirai export evidence/record --format junit xray testrail` (import files only, nothing is uploaded),
`tirai index evidence/ -o evidence/index.html` (one page for many runs).

To start from a written spec: `tirai from-spec login.feature --url <app url>` drafts the YAML (Gherkin, Markdown
or CSV tables); review every `TODO(...)` selector and the "not converted" lines with the user before recording.
Desktop apps: use a tab with `app:` (see docs/scenario-format.md, "Desktop apps").

## 4. Hand over

Give the user `final.mp4`, `report.html` (or `report.xlsx`) and `manifest.sha256`; `tirai verify` proves the files are unchanged. Check a few frames first
(`ffmpeg -ss <t> -i final.mp4 -frames:v 1 frame.png`) to confirm annotations and subtitles are visible.

## Ad-hoc annotation (outside a scenario)

`tirai annotate-js` prints the path of `annotate.js`. Inject it with
`agent-browser eval --stdin < <path>` then `agent-browser eval "__ann.arrow('#email',{label:'here'})"` (bsk: `bsk evaluate "$(cat <path>);..." --unverified`), clear with `__ann.clear()`.

---

## Source: skills/tirai-evidence/references/setup.md

# Setup

| OS | Install `tirai` + run `tirai setup` |
|---|---|
| macOS / Linux | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2tsoftwareapp/TIRAI/main/install.sh \| sh -s -- --yes` |
| Windows | `$env:TIRAI_SETUP_ARGS="--yes"; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2tsoftwareapp/TIRAI/main/install.ps1 \| iex` |

If `tirai` is already on PATH, run `tirai setup --yes` (add `--agent <name>` to choose agents).
It installs, with the OS package manager or official installer:

1. ffmpeg >= 6.0 (+ DejaVu font on Linux) — kept if new enough; otherwise a static build into `~/.tirai/bin`
   (Linux, Windows) or `brew install ffmpeg` (macOS).
2. agent-browser (default driver) — release binary into `~/.tirai/bin`, then `agent-browser install` (Chrome for Testing).
3. DBX web — `browser-static` release package into `~/.tirai/dbx` (Linux, Windows x64), else the Docker image.
4. BrowserSkill CLI (`bsk`) — Tencent's official `install.sh` / `install.ps1` into `~/.local/bin`.
5. The `tirai-evidence` skill for detected agents, plus BrowserSkill's own skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor.

Opt-in (only when the scenario needs them): `tirai setup --only ocr` (tesseract, for `privacy.ocr` /
`tirai scan-pii`), `--only voice` (espeak-ng on Linux; macOS `say` and Windows SAPI are built in) and
`--only agent-desktop` (desktop-app tabs with `app:`).

Manual steps the user must do (ask them; never automate):

- Only for `driver: bsk`: install the **BrowserSkill** extension from the Chrome Web Store or Edge Add-ons.
- For database tabs, start DBX web: `DBX_PASSWORD=... tirai dbx -d` (installed binary, or Docker)
  and create a connection with a **read-only** database user.

Finish with `tirai doctor` → `ready`. If Linux package installs need `sudo` and it asks for a password,
ask the user to run the printed command. Tool paths can be overridden with `FFMPEG_BIN`, `FFPROBE_BIN`, `AGENT_BROWSER_BIN`, `DBX_WEB_BIN`, `BSK_BIN`, `TIRAI_FONT`.

---

## Source: examples/demo/login-lock.yaml

```yaml
# Evidence scenario: each step = tab + actions + expect (+ annotations, subtitle).
# Run `tirai run --dry-run` first to find failing steps, then `tirai record`.
name: "Login validation + DB verification"
lang: en
tabs:
  app:
    url: ${APP_URL}
    label: "WEB APP"
  db:
    url: ${DBX_URL}
    label: "DATABASE (DBX)"
    kind: dbx          # enables the `sql:` action
    dbx:
      connect:         # create/update this DBX connection from databases.default before the tab opens
        name: shop-readonly
        host: evpg     # Postgres as DBX (in Docker) sees it
    setup:             # not recorded: login to DBX web once
      - dbx_login: "${DBX_PASSWORD}"

# Independent read-only check of the same data the DB tab shows (DBX renders results on a canvas).
databases:
  default:
    dsn: "${EV_DB_DSN}"

steps:
  - id: S1
    tab: app
    title: Open the login page
    subtitle: "Step 1: Open the application login page"
    actions:
      - navigate: ${APP_URL}
    expect:
      - visible: "#email"
      - text_contains: { selector: h2, text: "Sign in" }
    annotate:
      - box: { target: "form", label: "Login form", color: "#1f6feb" }

  - id: S2
    tab: app
    title: Invalid email format
    subtitle: "Step 2: Enter a malformed email → validation error"
    actions:
      - fill: { selector: "#email", value: "alice-at-demo.local" }
      - fill: { selector: "#password", value: "${APP_PASSWORD}" }
      - click: "button[type=submit]"
    expect:
      - text_contains: { selector: ".error", text: "Email format is invalid." }
    annotate:
      - box: { target: "#email" }
      - arrow: { target: ".error", from: right, label: "Invalid email format" }
      - blur: { target: "#password" }

  - id: S3
    tab: app
    title: Locked account is rejected
    subtitle: "Step 3: Log in as bob@demo.local (locked) → rejected"
    actions:
      - fill: { selector: "#email", value: "bob@demo.local" }
      - fill: { selector: "#password", value: "${APP_PASSWORD}" }
      - click: "button[type=submit]"
    expect:
      - text_contains: { selector: ".error", text: "This account is locked" }
    annotate:
      - circle: { target: ".error" }
      - arrow: { target: ".error", from: bottom, label: "Account locked" }
      - blur: { target: "#password" }

  - id: S4
    tab: db
    title: Database shows bob as LOCKED
    subtitle: "Step 4: Query the DB (read-only user): bob has status = LOCKED, failed_logins = 5"
    actions:
      - sql: "SELECT id, email, status, failed_logins FROM users WHERE email = 'bob@demo.local';"
    expect:
      - db:
          sql: "SELECT email, status, failed_logins FROM users WHERE email = 'bob@demo.local'"
          columns: [email, status, failed_logins]
          rows: [{ email: bob@demo.local, status: LOCKED, failed_logins: 5 }]
    annotate:
      - box: { target: ".cm-content", color: "#1f6feb", label: "Read-only query", labelPos: bottom }
      - highlight: { target: { grid: { column: status, row: 1 } } }
      - box: { target: { grid: { column: status, toColumn: failed_logins, row: 1 } }, padding: 2 }
      - arrow: { target: { grid: { column: status, toColumn: failed_logins, row: 1 } }, from: right, label: "status = LOCKED, failed_logins = 5" }

  - id: S5
    tab: app
    title: Valid login succeeds
    subtitle: "Step 5: Log in as alice@demo.local → dashboard"
    actions:
      - fill: { selector: "#email", value: "alice@demo.local" }
      - fill: { selector: "#password", value: "${APP_PASSWORD}" }
      - click: "button[type=submit]"
    expect:
      - url_contains: "/dashboard"
      - text_contains: { selector: "#welcome", text: "Welcome, Alice Nguyen" }
    annotate:
      - box: { target: "#welcome", color: "#16a34a", label: "Logged in", labelPos: bottom }

  - id: S6
    tab: db
    title: Database shows alice as ACTIVE
    subtitle: "Step 6: Query the DB: alice has status = ACTIVE"
    actions:
      - sql: "SELECT id, email, status, failed_logins FROM users WHERE email = 'alice@demo.local';"
    expect:
      - db:
          sql: "SELECT email, status FROM users WHERE email = 'alice@demo.local'"
          columns: [email, status]
          rows: [{ email: alice@demo.local, status: ACTIVE }]
    annotate:
      - highlight: { target: { grid: { column: status, row: 1 } }, color: "#22c55e" }
      - arrow: { target: { grid: { column: status, row: 1 } }, from: right, color: "#16a34a", label: "status = ACTIVE" }
```
